skill.name: monorepo-management
skill.description: Build efficient, scalable monorepos that enable code sharing, consistent tooling, and atomic changes across multiple packages and applications.
skill.summary: Plan, configure, optimize, and release JavaScript and TypeScript monorepos.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Monorepos become difficult when dependencies, builds, and releases lack consistent structure. This skill provides practical patterns for workspaces, caching, CI, and publishing.
actual_capabilities: Compares pnpm workspaces, Turborepo, Nx, and Lerna for common monorepo needs.
Provides workspace structures and configuration patterns for applications and shared packages.
Explains filtered dependency installation and task execution with pnpm.
Shows shared TypeScript, ESLint, UI, utility, and type package patterns.
Outlines caching, affected builds, parallel tasks, and GitHub Actions workflows.
Covers package versioning and publishing with Changesets.
limitations: The examples use specific tool versions that may require updates.
The skill does not inspect repositories or execute commands automatically.
Every configuration requires validation against the target repository and deployment environment.
Coverage focuses on JavaScript and TypeScript tools, not polyglot build systems.

use_cases.title: Design a New Workspace
use_cases.description: Choose a workspace layout, package boundaries, shared configuration, and build orchestration for a new product.

use_cases.title: Migrate Existing Repositories
use_cases.description: Plan an incremental migration that preserves releases while consolidating applications and shared libraries.

use_cases.title: Improve Build and Release Pipelines
use_cases.description: Configure caching, affected tasks, CI checks, versioning, and package publishing for faster delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Monorepo Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a monorepo for [applications] and [shared packages]. Recommend a workspace tool, directory structure, root scripts, and validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Starting a small JavaScript or TypeScript monorepo.

prompt_templates.title: Review Workspace Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my workspace structure and configuration. Identify dependency, caching, and script issues. Prioritize changes and include verification commands.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Repository Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an incremental migration from [repositories] into one monorepo. Preserve independent deployments, define package boundaries, and include rollback checkpoints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Consolidating several repositories without interrupting delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize CI and Releases
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an affected-only CI and release strategy for [toolchain]. Include cache inputs, dependency ordering, parallelism, Changesets, secret handling, and failure recovery.
prompt_templates.scenario: Scaling builds and package publishing across many projects.

output_examples.input: Plan a monorepo for a web application, documentation site, shared UI library, and shared TypeScript configuration.
output: Use separate applications and packages directories with explicit workspace boundaries.
Place reusable UI and TypeScript configuration in independently validated packages.
Add root build, test, lint, and type-check tasks with dependency-aware ordering.
Verify local builds before enabling remote caching.

output_examples.input: Improve slow CI for an Nx workspace with many unaffected projects.
output: Run affected targets against a reliable main-branch base reference.
Define complete cache inputs and outputs for each target.
Limit parallelism to available runner resources.
Track cache hit rates and compare pipeline duration after each change.

output_examples.input: Prepare shared packages for independent publishing.
output_examples.output: Introduce Changesets, document package ownership, validate dependency ranges, and test release automation in a non-production registry before publishing.

best_practices: Keep package dependencies explicit and the dependency graph acyclic.
Centralize shared tooling while allowing documented application-specific overrides.
Validate cache inputs, build outputs, affected logic, and release permissions in CI.
anti_patterns: Do not share unstable application code only to remove small duplication.
Do not rely on hoisted phantom dependencies that are absent from package manifests.
Do not enable remote caching or publishing before validating credentials and access boundaries.

faq.question: Which monorepo tools does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers pnpm workspaces, Turborepo, Nx, Lerna, GitHub Actions, and Changesets.

faq.question: Can it choose between Turborepo and Nx?
faq.answer: It can compare their documented strengths against your project size, workflow, and orchestration needs.

faq.question: Does it modify my repository?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples unless your agent receives a separate request and permission to edit files.

faq.question: Can it help migrate multiple repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure an incremental migration plan with package boundaries, deployment continuity, validation, and rollback checkpoints.

faq.question: Does it support package publishing?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Changesets workflows for creating versions, publishing packages, and integrating releases with GitHub Actions.

faq.question: What should I verify before using the examples?
faq.answer: Confirm current tool versions, repository paths, cache behavior, CI permissions, secret handling, and deployment requirements.
